title: Bloom filter
summary: Size a Bloom filter from a target item count and false-positive rate, derive k positions by double hashing, and measure the false-positive rate you actually get.

complexity.space: m = ⌈−n ln p / (ln 2)²⌉ bits, ≈ 9.6 bits per item at p = 1%

hints: A Bloom filter is m bits and k hash positions per item. add sets all k bits; a lookup says "maybe" only if all k are set, and "definitely not" if any one is clear.
Size it first: m = ceil(−n · ln p / (ln 2)²) and k = round((m / n) · ln 2), at least 1. Store the bits packed, 8 per byte: bit i lives in byte i >> 3 under mask 1 << (i & 7).
You don't need k hash functions. Compute h1 and h2 once (the two seeded hashes in the starter), then position i is (h1 + i · h2) mod m for i = 0 … k − 1.
